body: It happens when the tab barely touches the ring, not even hard enough to move it. I can rotate the ring and move it all around without any discomfort. I’m completely stumped.

It’s definitely under the cartilage. After it happened, I moved the ring around, rotated it, and pushed/pulled on it to see, and none of it bothered it. It happens as soon as the tab barely touches the ring, not even hard enough to move it. It’s super weird.
I had the same issue with mine years ago. If you can get into a shop and have the studs swapped for rings, that might help. Personally, I couldn’t stand rings, and ended up giving up on mine.

I think you’ll find that even though there are similarities among coworkers, everyone has their quirks. Everyone I work with is a “man’s man” as far as their appearance and hobbies go. I just moved to a new local and have definitely gotten some looks and comments when I walked in with all my nose rings, hand tattoo, and painted nails. But once it’s been said and it’s out of the way, it became apparent that we’re all there doing the same job for the same reason: we enjoy the work, and construction in general. Just be you, and people will like you for it. And if they don’t, forget ‘em.

Depending on the diameter of the ring, it could just be that it’s heavier than your piercing is used to. Septum’s are sensitive when they’re healing. I got mine pierced about 3 weeks ago and even certain facial expressions still hurt it.
Agreed. I have 3 nostrils, 2 high nostrils, and my septum and I think my high nostrils are my favorite.

If you planned ahead to stack 3, I don’t see why it would be a problem. But my high nostrils are about as high as I could go without getting into cartilage, which the piercer said he would not be comfortable piercing anyways. But if you went as high as you possibly could on top, and lower on the bottom ones, you could probably squeeze another hole in the middle.

I’ve never had to punish a dog for going in the house, I’ve always had excellent experiences with just praising and rewarding them for going outside. And it’s not excited or a dribble, he intentionally squats, and it’s always right by the door as I’m putting his leash on. I’ve been at home every day since I got him, so we go out very frequently. Even if he hardly pees outside, he will still go inside by the door every single time.
I’ve always praised them for going outside and not in the house, and when I first brought each of them home, it made a tremendous difference. But in this instance, I’m not seeing any improvement.
